an5.48:4.8: Note that the sense of visalla in such contexts is established at Thag 9.1 and SN 7.17 where it is associated with a forest.
an5.48:9.2: _Paveṇi_ appears only in this phrase in early Pali. It is explained by the commentary as “family customs”. But the root meaning is “weave, braid”, and it is known in Sanskrit as a woven rug that is a legitimate offering for brahmins. See [dn1:1.15.2]() and note.
